what: Writes every table in its one canonical form
how: tad canon rewrites each table's file - compact JSON lines, declared field order, empty as null, rows in their order - only when the data checks out.
why: A change reads as one line in a pull request.
evidence: Byte for byte as DuckDB wrote: Python's data unchanged, messy copies written identically (2026-11-11).

what: Checks every row and every rule across tables against the declaration
how: tad check reads tables.toml and data/: types, required fields, allowed values, patterns, ranges, keys, then unique ids, references, citations and mirrored relations across tables.
why: Nothing wrong reaches a commit: a bad row is named with its table and line.
evidence: The same verdicts as the Python engine on all four repositories and on sixteen broken copies (2026-11-11).

what: Keeps every repository on tad's latest release
how: Each repository installs its pinned release with bin/install-tad.sh after checking the checksum; the lab's weekly timer runs bin/update-pins.sh, which moves each pin, re-renders, records a glimpse and lands through that repository's CI.
why: Called, not copied: no copy drifts, and a new release reaches everyone checked.
evidence: All four repositories moved to 0.2.0, then 0.4.0, through their own CI (2026-11-11).
uses: bin/install-tad.sh, bin/update-pins.sh, consumers, the lab's timer

how: release-please keeps a release pull request from the commits; land merges it; the package conveyor builds x86_64 and aarch64 binaries, deb and rpm, with checksums and signed provenance, in the same run.
why: No version is bumped by hand, and every release can be verified.
evidence: tad 0.2.0, 0.3.0 and 0.4.0 released this way with no hand in it (2026-11-11).

what: Renders the data as documents, in Markdown and reStructuredText
how: tad render writes one page per table and an index, finding shapes in the data (relations, sources, grids, an about page) and reading any declared presentation.
why: The documents are always what the data says; CI requires them fresh.
evidence: 74 documents byte for byte as the Python renderer wrote them; the canon's pages from declared presentation identical but for the notice (2026-11-11, 2026-11-12).

what: Adds or changes one row, and keeps it only if every rule still holds
how: tad set TABLE --key ID --set field=value: typed by the declaration, dated if the table says so, then the whole repository checked; if anything breaks the file is put back and the problems named.
why: Nobody hand-edits a table, and a change that breaks a rule never lands.
evidence: An edit and an insertion identical to the Python engine's SQL (2026-11-11); a refused edit leaves the file untouched.

what: Answers SQL over the declared tables, through DuckDB
how: tad sql reads the declared tables into DuckDB (tad engine installs its pinned binary, fingerprint checked), runs the statement, and brings the tables back through tad's canonical form and checks - the third way into the same data, beside files and text.
why: SQL with joins is the reason tad exists (why-tad-exists); lab-agent's journal will be queried this way.
evidence: Proven equal to the Python engine's sql on all four repositories at their last commit with it (2026-11-12): zero diff on a no-op, the 13 former SQL checks alike on clean and broken data, the same join counts, byte-identical updates and insertions, breaking changes refused by both.

what: The guard and the one fixed form
how: Every edit is loaded, checked against the schema and its rules, and written back one way only; anything else fails.
why: A one-row change must be a one-line difference, or nobody can review it.

how: Data is changed through one runner with queries, never by hand in the files.
why: An edit by hand skips every rule.
